title: incremental-onboard-audit-and-changelog-curator
author: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Motivation: The current onboarding pipeline generates monolithic changelogs that are hard to reason about for incremental model updates and cause noisy release notes for downstream consumers. We need a smaller-footprint, deterministic audit trail for onboard mutations plus a curator that can assemble concise release notes by impact, dataset/capacity signals, and workload-relevance. This PR implements two coordinated pieces: 1) an incremental onboard audit worker that records compact, per-field deltas and stable provenance IDs; and 2) a changelog curator service that consumes audit fragments, attaches representative telemetry (sampled), and drafts reviewer-friendly release notes.

What this changes: single continuous implementation and tests described below. High-level features: deterministic fragment IDs (sha256 of canonicalized delta + onboarding-timestamp), delta types (metadata, binary, profile, compatibility), per-field confidence tokens, optional telemetry attachments (latency/cost histograms sampled from onboarding probes), CLI integration (mrctl release draft --from <tag> --to <tag> --cohort <cohort>), and a docs page describing the migration and review workflow.

Implementation notes: - added services/onboard_audit/worker.py: an async worker that listens to onboarding transactions and emits compact audit fragments into changelog_fragments table; uses protobuf-lite schema for compactness. - added services/changelog_curator/assembler.py: consumes fragments, groups by model family/variant, computes impact buckets (breaking, risky, safe), and renders markdown templated release notes. - DB migration db/migrations/20260220_add_onboard_audit.sql: creates changelog_fragments, audit_index, and a small provenance table. - CLI tools/mrctl/release.py: new subcommand to produce drafts and push to Linear as draft issues when run with --publish. - telemetry sampling implemented in services/onboard_audit/sampler.py using reservoir sampling + tenant-scoped hashed salt to avoid PII leakage. - tests: tests/integration/test_changelog_curator.py and tests/unit/test_fragment_id_determinism.py. - docs: docs/onboarding/release-notes.md and docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9876) - [x] Schema migration with backfill plan - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Security review (sampling privacy constraints) - [x] Docs and migration guide - [x] CLI integration - [x] CI green (see checks below)

Commit summary: "initial onboard audit worker and curator; migrations; CLI; tests; docs"

Notes on privacy: telemetry attachments are optional per-tenant and only include aggregated histograms. Sampling uses a salted hash to partition telemetry into deterministic cohorts without including raw identifiers. See docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md for tenants with strict telemetry disallow lists.

Backwards compatibility and migration: fragments are append-only and do not change existing model_profile blobs. A backfill job (provided as part of the migration) converts recent onboarding transactions into fragments; the curator can operate in read-only mode when fragments are not present (falls back to previous changelog generator). Migration instructions are in docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md.

Why this is unique: instead of producing a single changelog blob per release, we create small, queryable fragments that can be merged/curated per-consumer. This reduces noise for downstream services that only care about performance-profile changes or compatibility signals.

Testing and validation performed: unit tests for fragment id determinism, integration tests for end-to-end draft generation, manual run against staging onboard stream (internal run id: staging-20260224). CI ran coverage and a lightweight load test for the worker (target throughput 120 reqs/s with 50ms mean processing).

Rollout plan: feature-gate with tenant flag onboard_audit_v1; deploy worker and migrations during a low-traffic window; backfill windows run per-tenant with rate limits; promote curator to default once we observe stable churn for 48 hours.

Links: Design ticket: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9876/incremental-onboard-audit-and-changelog-curator, Staging run: internal:///runs/staging-20260224, Migration plan: docs/migrations/onboard-audit-migration.md

review_comments: Jae Park: Please ensure telemetry sampling can't be correlated back to tenant IDs. Can you add deterministic salt and document the privacy model?
Aisha Kapoor: Reply: added tenant-scoped salted hashing and documented behavior in migration guide. Sampling is opt-in per tenant. Updated sampler implementation and unit tests.
Marta Rossi: Migration steps look good but we need a clear rollback plan if the backfill fails mid-tier. Add step to mark fragments as partial and a resumable backfill token.
Aisha Kapoor: Added resumable backfill token and a 'partial_backfill' flag in the provenance table. Updated migration doc and backfill script.
Ethan Cole: Minor: please include an example of the CLI output for a small model family in docs/release-notes.md
Aisha Kapoor: Added CLI example and a sample output block to docs/onboarding/release-notes.md
Jae Park: CI green and privacy reviewer acked. Approving. 👍
Marta Rossi: Approved after docs update.
